Source and row verification
- Cited source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films, section "High-grossing films by year of release", locator lines 300-304 and 421-471 in the fetched page.
- The 15 CSV rows match the master table values after stripping currency symbols and comma separators. Key locators: 1980s rows at lines 421, 424, 426; 1990s rows at lines 436, 441, 443; 2000s rows at lines 447, 451, 454; 2010s rows at lines 460, 463, 464; 2020s rows at lines 466, 467, 470.
- The source's gross convention is re-release-inclusive: the master article says year-table grosses are not limited to original theatrical runs and first-run grosses appear in brackets when known (same URL, lines 300-301 and line 472). The CSV correctly uses the outer cumulative value, not the bracketed first-run value.
- Mechanical checks passed: 15 rows x 5 columns; CSV columns match draft.json::columns; composite PK (Decade, Rank Within Decade) is unique; source_count=1 equals len(source_urls); all required draft fields are present; required curation fields are present; normalization_decisions has 6 entries and open_questions has 7 entries; sort is Decade ASC then Rank Within Decade ASC; gross values descend inside every decade.
- Title preservation passed against the master visible text, including E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace with en dash, and Spider-Man: No Way Home.
- 1989 range handling is acceptable as documented. The master row shows Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade as a range (same URL, line 432), but the master references Box Office Mojo for the exact lower figure (same URL, line 1587), and Box Office Mojo shows worldwide all-releases gross $474,171,806 (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt0097576/, lines 31-41). The 1989-in-film Wikipedia page also lists Indiana Jones at $474,171,806 and Batman below it at $411,569,241 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_in_film, lines 410-413). Using the lower bound keeps Return of the Jedi at #3 for the 1980s; the alternative upper-bound scenario remains correctly documented as an open normalization risk.
- Wiki-family discovery did not find a more direct worldwide, per-decade top-3 Wikipedia/Wikidata source. The current cited master is still the direct source for worldwide year-leader data. Wikidata Q392108 only identifies the page as a Wikimedia list article/list of film and provides sitelinks, not row data (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q392108, lines 45 and 105-123). The U.S. yearly page is domestic-only and would change the metric, so it is not a missing ground-truth source for this worldwide instance.

Findings

1. Source-shape and temporal-scope prose needs a hygiene update. (scope-related, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)
The staged artifacts repeatedly describe the master table as 1 row per year and the in-scope source base as exactly 1980-2025 = 46 year-leaders, with 2026-2029 unknown. Evidence in staged files: draft.json temporal_note at datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/top_3_highest_grossing_films_per_decade_1980s_to_2020s.draft.json:30; curation.json source_coverage_notes at datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/top_3_highest_grossing_films_per_decade_1980s_to_2020s.curation.json:56-58 and decision_log at lines 140-165. The live master article is slightly messier: it says conflicting estimates can cause both films to be recorded (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films, lines 300-302), has two candidate entries under 1995 and 2005 in the fetched table (same URL, lines 438-450), and now includes a 2026 row (same URL, lines 465-471). This does not change the staged CSV: the duplicate-year candidate rows are below their decade top-3 thresholds, and the 2026 film's $967,649,170 is below the current 2020s #3 threshold of Spider-Man: No Way Home at $1,922,598,800. Minimal repair is to say the source has 46 release-year buckets through 2025 after resolving duplicate candidate rows to the relevant year leader, and to either freeze scope explicitly at 1980-2025 or refresh the partial-decade note to acknowledge the live 2026 row.

2. The documented gap-check contains inaccurate supporting details, though the row set remains correct. (factual, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE)
The curation gap-check says the 2010s #4 year-leader is Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 at $1.34B and says no 2010s #2-of-year film exceeded about $1.51B; it also says no 2020s #2-of-year film exceeded Inside Out 2's $1.70B level. Evidence in staged files: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/top_3_highest_grossing_films_per_decade_1980s_to_2020s.curation.json:45-50. The live master table shows The Avengers 2012 at $1,518,815,515, which is the #4 year-leader for the 2010s after Endgame, Force Awakens, and Infinity War (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films, lines 455-464). The master all-time chart also shows Jurassic World 2015 at $1,671,537,444 and The Lion King 2019 at $1,656,943,394, both non-year-leader 2010s films above the stated $1.51B cap but still below Infinity War (same URL, lines 196-199). For the 2020s, Zootopia 2 is a 2025 non-year-leader at $1,866,647,950, above Inside Out 2's $1,698,863,816 but still below Spider-Man: No Way Home (same URL, lines 190-195). No CSV row changes are needed, because none of these non-year-leader contenders exceeds the staged #3 threshold in its decade, but the false-negative proof should be corrected.

Non-finding checks
- operation_type=projection is acceptable under the current local vocabulary and local precedent for hierarchical top-K-per-partition instances. Aggregation would be worse because the table is not COUNT/SUM/MIN/MAX; it is a partitioned ranking/projection. Protocol locator: datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/curation_protocol.md:320-333. Local precedent: top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent.draft.json uses operation_type=projection for a similar partitioned rank shape.
- claim_type=source_defined is honest. No supplement rows are added; the row universe is a deterministic transformation of the cited master table values. The curation record should just clean up the duplicate-row/2026 prose noted above.
- domain=Culture/Film is correct under domain_taxonomy.md, which places film under Culture (datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/domain_taxonomy.md:36-38).
- entity class artifacts/films is consistent with the local answer-entity-wins policy for scaffold+rank PKs: Decade and Rank are structural axes, while Film is the answer entity. Locator: datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/instance_selection_priorities.md:1583-1593 and the per-instance inventory at lines 1747-1749.
- Rank Within Decade as numeric is acceptable because the cells are bare integers. If a repair pass is already editing the metadata, changing the column type to rank would be semantically cleaner per curation_protocol.md:274-279, but I am not counting this as a finding because numeric is still normalized and evaluator-safe.

Verdict
Ready / Not ready: Ready. There are zero BLOCKING findings.

3. Correct the gap-check: 2010s #4 year-leader is The Avengers 2012, and current nearest non-year-leader challengers include Jurassic World, The Lion King, and Zootopia 2; all remain below their decade #3 thresholds.
